uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast UK consumer prices are rising. The Bank of England targets it at 2%, so it moves rate expectations and the pound; the September figure also sets benefit uprating.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: Economists have warned of 5% UK inflation if a US diesel ban goes ahead, which makes this reading the starting point that fuel risk is measured from. It also arrives with Burnham's triple lock pledge under dispute: the September figure is one of the measures that sets what the pledge costs.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-10.recent: Most officials expect another hike by year-end, but the Labor Department counted 29,000 new jobs against 90,000 expected, and the committee is split over whether stalled hiring outweighs inflation that has topped its target for 5.5 years. It meets as Trump's panel hears Lisa Cook, a governor whose seat carries one of those votes.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The euro area's central bank, whose Governing Council meets eight times a year to set interest rates for every country sharing the euro. Its decisions move the currency and the cost of government debt from Germany to Italy.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Inflation jumped to 3.8% in September, after a hike officials judged proportionate and not yet restrictive. The meeting weighs how much further to go against the heaviest debts, France first, where Moulin says no rescue is needed yet. Nominations to replace Isabel Schnabel, its leading voice for tighter policy, close the day before.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-10.recent: Three sources say the board is weighing a declaration that underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal. Japanese yields have already jumped in a global bond sell-off, and Takaichi is arguing that a growth push will support trust in the yen. The meeting settles whether the bank says so in its own name.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: The Bank of England's committee meets to vote on its benchmark rate, and the decision settles what borrowers pay and savers earn until it next meets.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Most Federal Reserve officials expect another hike by year-end, and this is the last meeting where that can happen. The committee is split: inflation has topped its target for 5.5 years, yet the latest jobs count was 29,000 against 90,000 expected. Trump's panel on removing Lisa Cook puts one of its votes in question.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The US is using its presidency to push the G20 back to its original priorities, and Russia's sherpa has backed the effort. Leaders gather after a Trump-Xi summit and with a US-India trade deal that Greer says is not imminent, so the meeting settles how many of the other members sign up to the host's agenda.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets about every six weeks to set interest rates for the countries that share the euro. Its decisions reach mortgages, government borrowing costs and the euro's exchange rate.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Officials judged September's hike proportionate and said policy still does not restrict growth, with inflation at 3.8%, nearly double the target. The council meets weeks before Isabel Schnabel, its leading voice for tighter policy, leaves on 3 January, and Moulin has said France needs no help from the bank yet.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The Bank of England's committee meets to set its policy rate, and the decision settles what households and firms on floating-rate loans pay, and what savers earn, going into the new year.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Three sources say the Bank is weighing a declaration that underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal. Japanese yields jumped in a global bond sell-off, and Takaichi has vowed to watch the yen and inflation carefully while pinning trust in the currency on her growth push. This meeting settles whether the declaration becomes a decision.

fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what US households pay for a basket of goods and services. It is the inflation reading that moves Treasury yields, the dollar and expectations for Fed rates.
fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.recent: September hiring stalled at 29,000 jobs against 90,000 expected, yet most Federal Reserve officials still expect another rate hike by year-end, and they are split over it. This release is the inflation reading that argument turns on: it shows the Fed whether dearer crude has reached consumer prices while hiring weakens.

fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of the prices US producers receive for goods and services. It shows cost pressure before it reaches shop shelves, and feeds the inflation gauge the Federal Reserve targets.
fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports the prices producers received last month. The release settles whether cost pressure at the factory gate and in wholesale services is building or easing before it reaches consumers.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of what American shops, restaurants and online sellers took in. Consumer spending is about two-thirds of the US economy, so it moves growth forecasts, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.recent: The Census Bureau reports its first estimate of last month's US retail sales, with revisions to the months before it. The release settles whether household spending held up or slowed, the largest single input to the quarter's growth figure.
